07 — Example ​

Full, annotated implementation. Read it after kata submit 07 passes.

The compilable files are reference/ch07/agent/budget.go, reference/ch07/agent/events.go and reference/ch07/agent/cmd/agent/main.go. The loop and the provider are unchanged.

The shape ​

budget.go   EstimateTokens, Fit, WithBudget, budgetedProvider
events.go   three new fields and the budget event type
main.go     -max-context, and one wrapper around the provider

Step 1 — estimate everything that is sent ​

go
func EstimateTokens(msgs []Message, tools []ToolDef) int {
	bytes := 0
	for _, m := range msgs {
		bytes += len(m.Role) + len(m.Content) + 4
		for _, tc := range m.ToolCalls {
			bytes += len(tc.ID) + len(tc.Name) + len(tc.Arguments)
		}
	}
	for _, t := range tools {
		bytes += len(t.Name) + len(t.Description)
		if schema, err := json.Marshal(t.Parameters); err == nil {
			bytes += len(schema)
		}
	}
	return bytes / 4
}

Three decisions:

  • Tool calls inside messages count. An assistant message carrying a 3 KB argument string is not free, and neither is the tool result that follows it.
  • A fixed +4 per message. Every message carries a role and separators. Without it, a hundred empty messages estimate to zero.
  • One division at the end. Dividing per message rounds each cost down and under-counts long conversations badly.

Step 2 — fit from the newest end ​

go
kept := make([]Message, 0, len(rest))
for i := len(rest) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
	candidate := append([]Message{rest[i]}, kept...)
	trial := append(append([]Message{}, system...), candidate...)
	if len(kept) > 0 && EstimateTokens(trial, tools) > budget {
		break
	}
	kept = candidate
}

len(kept) > 0 is the guard that keeps at least one message. Without it, a single message bigger than the budget produces an empty conversation, and the model gets a system message and nothing to do.

Recomputing the estimate per candidate is O(n²) in the worst case. For a conversation of a few hundred messages that is microseconds, and it is much easier to get right than incremental accounting. Say so in a comment if you rewrite it.

Step 3 — repair the boundary ​

go
for len(kept) > 0 && kept[0].Role == RoleTool {
	kept = kept[1:]
	dropped++
}

Walking backwards means the cut can land between an assistant message and the tool results that answer it. A tool result whose call is missing makes the request invalid: providers reject it with a message about orphaned tool calls.

The cheapest correct fix is to drop the orphan. The alternative, pulling its call back in, can exceed the budget again.

Step 4 — one marker, not one per drop ​

go
if dropped > 0 {
	out = append(out, Message{
		Role:    RoleSystem,
		Content: fmt.Sprintf("[context pruned: %d earlier messages omitted to fit %d tokens]", dropped, budget),
	})
}

A system-role message is used because inserting a second user message changes the shape of the conversation, and a user message in the middle of history is a lie about who said what.

The number is included so a person reading -events output can see the difference between "one message was enormous" and "thirty messages were trimmed".

Step 5 — the decorator ​

go
func (b *budgetedProvider) Stream(ctx context.Context, req Request, onText func(string)) (Message, Usage, error) {
	b.calls++

	fitted, pruned := Fit(req.Messages, req.Tools, b.budget)
	b.emit(Event{
		Type:   EventBudget,
		Turn:   b.calls,
		Tokens: EstimateTokens(fitted, req.Tools),
		Budget: b.budget,
		Pruned: pruned,
	})

	req.Messages = fitted
	return b.inner.Stream(ctx, req, onText)
}

req is passed by value, so reassigning req.Messages affects only this call. That matters: the loop keeps its own history and must not be silently truncated by a request that mutated it.

budgetedProvider implements both Chat and Stream, so it satisfies StreamingProvider. Chat delegates to Stream, which means the budget applies to whichever entry point the caller uses.

Step 6 — wiring order ​

go
tools := agent.NewRegistry(...)

provider := agent.WithBudget(
	agent.NewOpenAICompat(baseURL, key, model),
	tools, *maxContext, emit,
)

The decorator needs the tool schemas, so tools are built first. That ordering is the only structural change in main.

WithBudget returns the provider unchanged when budget <= 0, which makes -max-context 0 mean "off" rather than "budget of zero tokens".

The diffs ​

1. Counting only messages — estimate-counts-tools

diff
- for _, m := range msgs { bytes += len(m.Content) }
+ for _, t := range tools { bytes += len(t.Name) + len(t.Description) + len(schema) }

2. Threshold instead of ceiling — ceiling-respected

diff
- if EstimateTokens(history) > budget { history = Fit(history) }   // once, at start
+ // inside the provider decorator, on every request

3. Dividing per message — estimate-grows-with-history

diff
- total += (len(m.Content) + 4) / 4
+ bytes += len(m.Content) + 4; ... ; return bytes / 4

4. Ignoring the orphan — no-orphaned-tool-pairs

diff
- return append(system, kept...)
+ for len(kept) > 0 && kept[0].Role == RoleTool { kept = kept[1:]; dropped++ }

Comparison checklist ​

  • [ ] estimate counts messages, tool calls and tool schemas
  • [ ] one division by four, at the end
  • [ ] system message kept and excluded from the walk
  • [ ] newest messages kept, at least one always
  • [ ] leading tool results dropped after the cut
  • [ ] one marker message naming the count and the budget
  • [ ] budget applied per request through a provider decorator
  • [ ] budget <= 0 disables rather than empties
  • [ ] event reports tokens, budget and pruned per request

Differences outside this list are style.
